title: Critique of Pure Inference: The Formation of Objects, the Conditions of Warrant, and the Standing of Conclusions
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A treatise on the entitlement to conclude. An inference can be valid inside a representation that has lost its object, and a sound inference can be repeated through citation, teaching, summary and machine composition until it is received as a datum and its step can no longer be seen; the repeated conclusion is a settlement. The work takes as its unit the whole passage from evidence through admission and representation to conclusion, public standing and revision. Part I derives the conditions of warrant and grades mediation after Kant and Hegel. Part II explains the illusions, the disciplinary, public, platform and liability interfaces, the composition layer and the inferential mathematics of the language model that executes the residue, and gives a history of how bad inference came to be operative in four stages (construal, count, standing, execution), read from seated witnesses: Irenaeus's ἑωράθη through Eusebius, the Latin version, Charles and a captured machine audit, with the exact sciences from Copernicus to Gödel as controls. Part III gives cases, an executable instrument, the protocol construal before count and a Doctrine of Method. Part IV draws the consequences and constructs materially sustained corrigibility, the capacity of a public practice to let a warranted correction change what it bears on, survive ordinary use and remain open to its own future critic. Version 1.2 (14 November 2026, in place) adds the reception history of §11.5–11.6, read from the witnesses seated for it in EA-CORPORA-38 (#1768). It follows six operations of the Peripatetic logic, among them the companions' modal rule, Theophrastus's added moods and the distinction between a method and a stock of reduced arguments, from Alexander to Frege. It shows them preserved, reassigned, rejected and made productive again. Kant's 1762 reduction of the fourth figure reproduces the Theophrastean placement without the name, and the account of logic in which the completion sentence of 1787 stands has no place for that placement as a contribution.
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). By Lee Sharks. Composed with ChatGPT (LABOR) and Claude (TACHYON) under the author's direction across working drafts v0.1–v0.10 (13 November 2026), with each external claim and quotation checked against its source or a seated text before entry; the development record (Appendix B) records which pass contributed what, and the countermodels in §8 were checked by direct calculation.
methodology: Close reading of the load-bearing loci in their original languages from seated texts (Irenaeus in Greek and Latin, Eusebius, Charles 1920, Kant AA III, Bacon, Copernicus 1543, Kepler 1609, Newton 1687, Einstein 1905, Heisenberg 1925, Gödel 1930 with the Königsberg issue), with line references to the seats; dated machine compositions kept whole in the Capture Registry; current research read at the depth stated in the research ledger (Appendix C); the model's objective, gradient, attention, decoding, post-training and in-context updating stated in their formulas, with constructed countermodels computed directly.
falsification_conditions: §12.9: the empirical scope contracts if the proposed transformations do not reproduce outside the selected archive cases, if ostensibly independent instances share only the critique's preferred descriptions, or if receiving contexts consistently supply the conditions alleged to be missing; the instrument fails where readers cannot apply its distinctions more reliably than unstructured judgment; the analytic claims fail on a procedure that, restricted to a representation erasing a decisive difference, still guarantees the distinction without further information, or on a bare repetition of an endorsement that contributes an independent observation by occurring.

wiki_article: Critique of Pure Inference is a treatise by Lee Sharks, deposited as version 1.0 on 13 November 2026 and composed with ChatGPT (LABOR) and Claude (TACHYON) under his direction. Its object is the entitlement to conclude. It holds that an inference can be valid inside a representation that has lost its object, and that a sound inference can be repeated through citation, teaching, summary and machine composition until it is received as a datum, which the work calls a settlement. Part I derives conditions of warrant after Aristotle, Kant and Hegel. Part II reads the disciplinary, public, platform and liability interfaces and the composition layer by one standard, states the training objective, gradient, attention, decoding, preference optimization and in-context updating of the language model in their formulas, and writes the history of how bad inference came to be operative in four stages, construal, count, standing and execution, from Irenaeus's unexpressed subject ἑωράθη through Eusebius, the Latin version, R. H. Charles and a captured machine audit, with Copernicus, Kepler, Newton, Einstein, Heisenberg and Gödel as cases where the object broke the settlement. Part III gives the instrument, the protocol construal before count and a Doctrine of Method. Part IV draws consequences from The Final Time and constructs materially sustained corrigibility. It applies its standard to the archive that runs it. Version 1.2 (14 November 2026) adds a reception history read from witnesses seated for it. Alexander of Aphrodisias and Philoponus carry the companions' arguments; Boethius names Theophrastus and Eudemus for five added moods; Meier's handbook teaches them as Galen's figure; Kant in 1762 reduces that figure to the first, where Theophrastus had placed the moods; Peirce restores the name; and the Nyāyasūtra serves as the control, keeping doubt and purpose in the inquiry while excluding them from the proof.

defines_concepts.definition: In Critique of Pure Inference, the claim that an inferential operation supplies its own sufficient warrant for the selection, representation and public standing of its object, and, in its second form, the claim that a conclusion's standing is established by its repetition.

In Critique of Pure Inference §11.3, the protocol by which every open place in a cited witness is located, each construal stated and tested on the same terms, and the witness counted only afterwards, under one construal and once with its dependents.

In Critique of Pure Inference §15, the capacity of a public knowledge practice to receive a warranted challenge, determine what it bears on, change the decisions it bears on, preserve that change across ordinary use, and maintain the carriers and labour required to do so.

In Critique of Pure Inference §11.0j and §8.11–8.23, the language model as it takes the accrued residue of historical inferential reasoning and wields it according to the operations of deduction, often without inferring over the object itself.
